text:
alex: FYI seeing a p95 spike on node-local DNS in the gpu-pool (us-west-2) starting ~08:12 UTC — resolves from 600ms -> 3s and ~5% timeouts. This is impacting grpc calls between model-worker pods.

infra-bot: [ALERT] node-local-dns: p95 resolve latency > 1s on nodes: gpu-*-usw2 (alert id dns-2065).

maria: Any signs of increased drop/jitter on east-west links? RDMA/MTU related?

jordan: I pulled a tcpdump from one affected node during a timeout window. see snippet:```
08:12:34.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.53 > 10.0.7.45.50923: UDP, length 512
08:12:34.123789 IP 10.0.7.45.50923 > 10.0.5.53: UDP, length 128
... repeated fragments, then nothing (no reply)
```

jordan: Also seeing lots of fragmented UDP reassembly failures in kernel logs: "UDP: bad checksum, dropping" on nodes attached to RDMA NICs.

maria: That matches suspicion — RDMA NIC offloads + jumbo MTU mismatch across some switches is causing fragmented DNS UDP packets to get dropped. We've hit this before with grpc tail latency.

alex: Good call. Quick mitigation options?

maria: Short-term: disable GRO/GSO on the NICs for the node-local-dns traffic interface, e.g.:```
ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
```

maria: Medium-term: standardize MTU across the fabric or force DNS to use TCP fallback where possible + increase node-local cache to reduce query volume.

jordan: I can roll a one-off kube-daemonset patch to bump node-local-dns cacheSize and reduce its upstream timeout. Proposed config fragment:```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  cacheSize: "4096"
  upstreamTimeoutMs: "300"
```
```
(not exact keys, but will PR proper values)
```

alex: Can we also route DNS traffic off the RDMA network for now? e.g., taint/tolerate or use a nodeSelector to prefer standard ENI-based nodes for dns.

maria: Yes — we have a small non-RDMA nodepool (cpu-only). We can patch node-local-dns to prefer those nodes by affinity for the short term.

sre-oncall: I'll schedule a rolling patch window for 09:30 UTC to: 1) disable GRO/GSO on affected NICs, 2) patch node-local-dns daemonset to prefer non-RDMA nodes + bump cache, 3) run iperf/packetloss matrix across AZs.

jordan: For diagnostics, run these on a pod on both sides:```
# check path MTU and reassembly
ping -s 1472 -M do <peer-ip>
# iperf UDP test
iperf3 -c <peer> -u -b 100M -t 30
# capture fragments
tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/dns-frags.pcap 'udp port 53'
```

alex: One more ask — add CoreDNS metrics for "udp_fragment_drops" to the dashboard so we can see this signal earlier.

maria: Agreed. Also opening a vendor ticket with NIC vendor to check RDMA firmware + offload semantics.

infra-bot: [INCIDENT] Created incident INC-206543 (node-local-dns_eastwest_rdma_jitter). Pager duty notified.

sre-oncall: Action items: 
• jordan: PR node-local-dns config changes (cache + upstream timeout) — due 09:00 UTC
• maria: prep ethtool disable playbook + non-RDMA affinity change — due 09:15 UTC
• alex: dashboard update for udp_fragment_drops + alert threshold — due 10:00 UTC
• ops: run cross-AZ iperf+ping matrix and attach pcaps to incident.

alex: Thanks — we'll try the NIC offload disable first and monitor. :thumbsup:
